jobs.title: Public Sector Strategy Project Manager
jobs.description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:

At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.

In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence

About The Role

The California State Controller’s Office (SCO) is currently implementing a large and complex SaaS solution to support the California State Payroll System (CSPS) project. CSPS is a massive project, and the implementation includes both Personnel and Payroll functionality to support the needs of some 300,000 employees across 160 agencies and 21 bargaining units. With an estimated project budget exceeding $1 billion and staffing approaching 200 IT professionals, this highly complex effort is expected to continue for the next several years.

Description

The Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for execution, maintenance and enhancement of the CSPS Project Management Plans.

PMO responsibilities include:

ensuring that formal PM processes are in place and followed across all project workstreams (leadership, functional, technical, and organizational change management)
ensuring documentation is maintained in accordance with policy and procedure
regular periodic reporting on project risks, issues, and overall health, including stakeholder presentations as needed
assisting the CSPS Leadership Team in monitoring system integrator performance
providing analysis and recommendations for improvements to project management processes

The CSPS PMO is currently staffed by four senior project managers who each work directly with a state and system integrator counterpart.

Contract Required Qualifications For The Senior Project Manager Role

Requires a minimum of seven (7) years of broad, extensive and increasingly responsible experience applying PM principles, methods, techniques, and tools. At least four (4) years of that experience must have been as a senior PM of one or more large or complex IT projects.

Possession of (a) a bachelor’s degree, and (b) a valid Project Management Professional (PMP) certification from the Project Management Institute (PMI)

Additional qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis. The PMP certification is required and may not be substituted with additional experience.

Additional Qualifications

The Senior PM role requires proven project management skills in a highly complex and large-scale IT implementation. The successful candidate will need to work well in a dynamic environment, providing exceptional client service with outstanding professionalism. The role requires direct interaction with client and system integrator staff, as well as:

Strong analytical, organizational and core project management skills
Ability to help client personnel to leverage technology to solve business problems
Strong verbal and written communication skills with a commitment to client service and professionalism
Possess conceptual thinking skills, creativity and flexibility
Work well both independently and in a team
Must be self-sufficient and have the ability to self-manage
Experienced and comfortable in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio)
Ability to learn quickly and adapt with other technology applications in day-to-day work

Other

Candidates will need to complete and pass a background check conducted by SCO prior to beginning work
Remote work is allowed, but staff must be based in the continental United States. With advance notice, project staff will occasionally need to travel to Sacramento for project meetings.
Normal working hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific time. All staff, regardless of location, are required to perform duties within those hours.

We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Crowe, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,400.00 - $205,300.00 per year.

Our Benefits:

Your exceptional people experience starts here. At Crowe, we know that great people are what makes a great firm. We care about our people and offer employees a comprehensive total rewards package. Learn more about what working at Crowe can mean for you!

How You Can Grow:

We will nurture your talent in an inclusive culture that values diversity. You will have the chance to meet on a consistent basis with your Career Coach that will guide you in your career goals and aspirations. Learn more about where talent can prosper!

More about Crowe:

Crowe provides professional services through two separate entities: Crowe LLP delivers audit and attest services, and Crowe Advisory LLC provides tax, advisory, consulting, and other nonattest services.

The Crowe Global network consists of more than 300 independent accounting and advisory services firms in more than 150 countries around the globe, making it one of the largest accounting networks in the world*. As independent members of Crowe Global, Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC serve clients worldwide. (*As of July 2026)

Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC (and their respective subsidiary entities) provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetics, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC (and their respective subsidiary entities) does not accept unsolicited candidates, referrals or resumes from any staffing agency, recruiting service, sourcing entity or any other third-party paid service at any time. Any referrals, resumes or candidates submitted to Crowe, or any employee or owner of Crowe without a pre-existing agreement signed by both parties covering the submission will be considered the property of Crowe, and free of charge.

Crowe will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act.

Please visit our webpage to see notices of the various state and local Ban-the-Box laws and Fair Chance Ordinances, where applicable.

We are committed to a merit-based hiring process, evaluating all candidates consistently using objective, job-related criteria such as relevant experience, demonstrated skills, measurable impact, and alignment with the role’s responsibilities, and making employment decisions in a fair and inclusive manner free from discrimination.

If you are interested in applying for employment with Crowe and are in need of an accommodation or require special assistance to navigate our website or to complete your application, please visit our Applicant Assistance and Accommodations page for more information: https://careers.crowe.com/crowe-applicant-assistance-and-accommodation

jobs.title: Senior Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
An established technology business specialising in retail ERP solutions is looking for an experienced Senior Technical Project Manager
to oversee project delivery and team management across one of its key product streams.

Working with the PMO, you'll help guide your assigned product stream and oversee multiple projects through to delivery. You'll lead an onshore and offshore team across Project Management, Business Analysis, Development and DevOps, with responsibility for performance management, resource coordination and team development, while maintaining strong client and stakeholder relationships.

Salary:
180 -190k + super

Location:
NSW, 2127

Work arrangement:
Permanent role, hybrid (3 days p/w in office)

Key Responsibilities

Manage multiple projects concurrently, from requirements gathering and planning through to deployment and hypercare.
Oversee project scope, schedules, budgets, resources and delivery risks, ensuring projects meet agreed objectives.
Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team of Project Managers, Business Analysts, Developers and DevOps professionals across onshore and offshore locations.
Manage team performance, including setting performance plans, conducting annual reviews and supporting ongoing professional development.
Provide coaching, mentoring and direction to team members, building capability and encouraging a collaborative, cross-skilled team.
Coordinate internal resources and external stakeholders to manage competing priorities and ensure successful project delivery.
Build strong relationships with customers and senior stakeholders, acting as a key point of contact throughout the project lifecycle.
Monitor project progress, manage changing requirements and address delivery challenges as they arise.
Prepare and present project updates, risks and delivery progress to senior management.
Identify opportunities to improve project delivery processes, team performance and ways of working.

About You

At least 5 years' experience managing projects in a technical environment.
Previous experience leading multidisciplinary teams, including Developers, DevOps, Business Analysts and Project Managers, across onshore and offshore locations.
Confident managing people, including performance plans, annual reviews, coaching and development.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build relationships with internal teams, senior stakeholders and external clients.
Resilient, patient and adaptable, with the ability to navigate challenges and keep projects moving when things don't go to plan.
Experience working across Agile and Waterfall environments, with strong knowledge of JIRA and Confluence.
Project Management qualifications such as PMP or PRINCE2, or relevant industry experience.
Experience within automotive retail, Dealer Management Systems (DMS) or ERP environments would be highly regarded.

What's On Offer

The opportunity to take ownership of a key development stream within an established technology business.
A senior leadership position combining project delivery, people management and stakeholder engagement.
Exposure to large-scale technology projects and the evolving automotive retail industry.
Flexible working arrangements, with a minimum of three days per week in the office.
Interstate travel and the opportunity to work closely with customers across Australia and New Zealand.

Sound like you? Apply now!

jobs.title: Solutions Senior Program Manager and Product Lifecycle Stewardship
jobs.description:
Description -

Solutions Program Manager:

Manage portfolio development across multiple Solutions, collaborating with Product Management prioritizing features, capabilities, and investment decisions.
Coordinate with NPI and Solutions program managers to drive integration of core solutions across product platforms.
Partner with Lead Architects and Technologists to drive innovation creating customer value and enhanced experiences across the Portfolio.
Work with Directors across Print, IQ, SW and Service organizations to coordinate key Solution and program deliveries.

Define program strategy, objectives, milestones, and success metrics aligned with business goals.
Translate customer and business requirements into actionable solution roadmaps and development plans.
Lead end-to-end delivery of AI-powered solutions from ideation through release and deployment.
Drive cross-functional execution across Product Management, Print Engineering, Data Telemetry, UX, Software, Firmware, Cloud, and Fleet Manageability teams.
Translate customer and business requirements into actionable solution roadmaps and development plans.
Ensure compliance with responsible AI, privacy, security, legal, and regulatory requirements.
Monitor program health, budget, schedules, resource allocation, and dependencies.
Communicate executive-level status, risks, and strategic recommendations to leadership.
Lead customer engagements, pilot programs, proof-of-concepts, and production rollouts.

Product Development Lifecycle

Own the Enterprise Product Development Lifecycle (PLC) framework from concept through end-of-life.
Define and maintain lifecycle processes, phase-gate requirements, deliverables, and governance standards.
Lead a cross-functional team of product stewards across the companies General Business Units for coordinating key updates to the Pan Print PLC.
Drive consistency across multiple product portfolios, business units, and development organizations.
Ensure cross-functional alignment on product development methodology, roles, responsibilities, and decision authority.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on accelerating time-to-market while maintaining quality and compliance.
Establish governance, risk management, key checkpoints and escalation frameworks for the business.
Evaluate current development processes and identify opportunities for simplification, automation, and scalability.
Lead process transformation initiatives supporting Agile, Hybrid, and Stage-Gate development methodologies.
Implement best practices for Program Management, governance, product planning, and execution.
Drive adoption of new tools, workflows, and operating models.
Facilitate organizational change management associated with process improvements.

Education & Experience Recommended

Four-year or Graduate Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or any other related discipline or commensurate work experience or demonstrated competence.
Typically has 10+ years of work experience, preferably in engineering development and implementation, project planning tools and software packages, people management, or a related field.
Exceptional communicator with strong presentation skills and the ability to lead through influence across diverse professional styles and cross- functional teams.
Proven "growth mindset" with a passion for technology and a deep understanding of the product lifecycle from initial design through end-of-life.
Experience working in complex, global, and cross-functional environments

Impact & Scope

Impacts large functions and leads large, cross-division functional teams or projects.

Complexity

Provides highly innovative solutions to complex problems within established policy.

Pay & Benefits

The pay range for this role is $147,050 to $230,850 USD annually with additional

opportunities for pay in the form of bonus and/or equity (applies to United

States of America candidates only). Pay varies by work location, job-related

knowledge, skills, and experience.

HP offers a comprehensive benefits package for this position, including:

Health insurance
Dental insurance
Vision insurance
Long term/short term disability insurance
Employee assistance program
Flexible spending account
Life insurance
Generous time off policies, including;
4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure
11 paid holidays
Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave

jobs.title: Project Manager/Site Engineer
jobs.description:
Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the worldâs most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

Shape the future of infrastructure with AECOM.

At AECOM, we’re delivering a better world. From roads and bridges to major transport and infrastructure programs, we’re working with clients, communities and partners to solve some of the world’s most complex challenges.

We’re looking for an experienced Project Manager/Site Engineer to join our team and play a key role in delivering high-quality civil infrastructure projects across the region.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of projects from planning and mobilisation through to delivery and close-out, working alongside some of the industry’s leading technical specialists and project professionals. You’ll bring strong project management capability, commercial awareness and a collaborative leadership style to deliver outcomes that make a real difference to the communities we serve.

What you’ll do

As a Project Manager, you’ll take a leading role in the successful delivery of infrastructure projects, balancing technical, commercial, safety, quality and stakeholder requirements to achieve outstanding project outcomes.

You’ll:

Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of civil infrastructure projects, ensuring they are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to the required quality standards.
Provide strong project leadership across the project lifecycle, from early planning and constructability through to construction, commissioning and close-out.
Work closely with clients, contractors, consultants and internal technical teams to establish clear project objectives and drive successful delivery.
Proactively identify and manage project risks, issues, opportunities and dependencies, taking action early to keep projects on track.
Oversee project budgets, forecasting, cash flow, resources and commercial performance, using data and insight to support effective decision-making.
Lead project planning and programming, ensuring resources, procurement and delivery strategies are aligned with project requirements.
Manage contracts and commercial relationships, supporting effective administration, change management, claims and dispute resolution where required.
Establish and maintain strong project governance, reporting and controls to provide clients and leadership with confidence in project performance.
Champion quality, health and safety, sustainability and risk management across project delivery.
Build trusted relationships with clients and stakeholders, providing practical advice and solutions to complex project and delivery challenges.
Lead and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, creating an inclusive environment where people can perform at their best.
Identify opportunities to improve project delivery, systems and processes and contribute to the continued growth and success of AECOM’s infrastructure business.

Qualifications

What you’ll bring

We’re looking for someone who combines strong project management capability with a genuine passion for delivering infrastructure that benefits communities.

You’ll ideally have:

A degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline, recognised by Engineers Australia.
Demonstrated experience managing the delivery of civil infrastructure projects, with experience across roads, bridges or transport infrastructure with Transport for Main Roads (TMR) highly regarded.
Experience across project development, construction delivery and contract administration.
Strong understanding of civil construction methodologies, road and bridge design, construction, maintenance and materials.
Experience managing project budgets, programs, resources, risks and commercial outcomes.
Experience working with major contract forms such as AS 2124, AS 4300, D&C, Alliance or similar contracting models is desirable.
Strong understanding of project governance, quality, safety and risk management.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships at all levels.
Strong commercial awareness and the confidence to make sound, timely decisions in a complex project environment.
A collaborative approach and the ability to bring multidisciplinary teams together around a common goal.
A commitment to creating a safe, inclusive and high-performing project environment.

RPEQ registration, or the ability to obtain RPEQ, will be highly regarded.

Additional Information

Why AECOM?

You’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the region’s most significant infrastructure projects while being part of a truly global organisation.

At AECOM, you’ll work alongside talented engineers, planners, project managers, designers and technical specialists who are passionate about creating a better future. We bring together diverse perspectives and expertise to solve complex problems and deliver outcomes that matter.

You’ll also have access to industry-leading technical expertise, career development opportunities and a global network of professionals who can support you to grow your career.

We believe infrastructure is about more than what we build. It’s about connecting people, enabling communities and creating places where people can thrive.

AECOM – where your ideas can make a difference

If you’re ready to take the next step in your project management career and help deliver the infrastructure that will shape our future, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now and bring your expertise to AECOM.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which we, our clients and our communities live and work around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. We are committed to connecting to Country in our work through meaningful engagement with First Nations peoples and businesses. Find out more about our Australian Reconciliation Action Plan here: https://aecom.com/au/our-vision-for-reconciliation/.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion – a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation and benefits programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We also provide a robust global well-being program. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager - Quote to Order
jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries outrun - leaner and cleaner. Here, progress is an expectation - for you, your team, and the world. As a global market leader, we’ll give you what you need to make it happen. It won’t always be easy, growing takes grit. But at ABB, you’ll never run alone. Run what runs the world.

This role sits within ABB's Robotics business, a leading global robotics company. We're entering an exciting new chapter as we’ve announced the plan for SoftBank Group to acquire ABB Robotics. SoftBank is a globally recognized technology group and investor/operator focused on AI, robotics, and next-generation computing. By joining us now, you’ll be part of a pioneering team shaping the future of robotics—working alongside world-class experts in a fast-moving, innovation-driven environment.

This Position Reports To

Business Process Manager

We Are Hiring 3 Implementation Managers To Drive Our Global Quote-to-Order Transformation. You Will Join a Key Initiative To Standardize Commercial Processes And Digital Solutions Across Our Business. Apply For The Region That Matches Your Profile And Career Aspirations

Europe — Flexible location across European countries
America — Flexible location across American countries
Asia — Flexible location across Asia (excl. China)

Each role is autonomous and high-impact, with direct influence on how our commercial operations work in your region.

About The Role

Join ABB Robotics as an Implementation Manager and drive the implementation and adoption of our global Quote-to-Order process and supporting digital solutions.

The role will work closely with country commercial organizations to understand their current ways of working, introduce the global Quote-to-Order process, identify gaps and local requirements, and support countries through the transition to the target process and tools. The current solution landscape includes CPQ and the commercial Quote-to-Order processes interfacing with SAP S/4HANA
, together with other supporting applications. The scope may evolve as the Quote-to-Order process and application landscape develops. The position is part of the Commercial Excellence – Quote to Order Process
organization and reports to the Quote to Order Process Manager
.

This is a high-impact, cross-functional role at the heart of our commercial transformation.

What You Will Do

Lead implementation of the global Quote-to-Order process across your region.
Facilitate workshops to map current country processes against the global target, identify gaps, and define how they are resolved.
Support countries through a complete tool landscape transformation — you'll be equally comfortable helping teams understand new processes and navigating new tools.
Act as the primary business process advisor and second-level tool support contact for your region's countries — balancing process discipline with pragmatic tool troubleshooting
Coordinate deployment of CPQ and related solutions, including the commercial process integration and handover into SAP S/4HANA.
Act as the primary Quote-to-Order implementation contact for your region’s countries, building trusted relationships with sales organizations and key stakeholders.
Build strong relationships with country Sales organizations and key stakeholders. Understand existing country commercial processes, requirements and ways of working and support countries through the change management process.
Define and execute country implementation plans covering preparation, testing, training, go-live and stabilization. Coordinate user acceptance testing and implementation readiness with countries and IT/IS teams.
Champion continuous improvement post go-live, translating recurring business challenges into structured requirements for process and tool enhancements.

What You Bring

3-5 years of proven experience in commercial process implementation, digital transformation or business change roles in a B2B environment.
Good understanding of commercial processes such as quotation, pricing, configuration, sales operations or order handling.
Experience working with commercial platforms such as CPQ, CRM, CLM or ERP is an advantage.
Experience with commercial processes integrated with SAP S/4HANA or comparable ERP environments is an advantage.
Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills. You are equally confident with business and technical audiences.
Experience working across multiple countries and in matrix organizations; structured, self-driven and ownership-oriented.
Fluent in English; local or regional language skills are an advantage. Willingness to travel frequently within your region, particularly during implementation phases.

The Ideal Candidate

You combine commercial understanding, process orientation and change management expertise. You know how to sit with a country team, understand how they work today, and guide them confidently toward a standardized global process, without losing sight of legitimate local needs. You do not need to be a Process Owner, CPQ specialist or ERP expert, but you must have enough breadth across commercial, process and systems topics to lead implementation to successful adoption.

jobs.description:
Overview

We are seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to drive technical strategy, infrastructure planning, and cross-functional execution across our LLM inference platform.

In this role, you will lead end-to-end programs spanning GPU capacity planning, inference optimization, model migrations, and cost-per-token efficiency, while building standardized benchmarking frameworks and governance policies to evaluate, select, and scale open-weight models safely across the organization. The scope will evolve as the platform and industry mature, so success requires strong technical judgment, structured execution, and comfort operating in ambiguity.

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

Set a long-term strategy and roadmap for the open-weight LLM inference platform. Base it on business goals, customer needs, barriers to adoption and industry trends, and build it with stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Security and Finance.
Turn business goals into ranked technical problems, such as cost per token, latency, throughput, reliability and model coverage.
Define and run programs for GPU capacity planning, inference optimization, model migrations, high availability and performance.
Build a consistent way to benchmark and evaluate open-weight models, covering serving performance, quality and cost.
Give leadership and teams data-backed recommendations for model selection.
Work with Security, Legal and Compliance on the policies and security requirements that let teams adopt open-weight and OSS models safely.
Partner with and influence engineers, ML engineers and architects to settle trade-offs and keep programs moving.
Own programs end to end, from initiation through forecasting, budgeting and scheduling to delivery, including inference cost models.
Manage complex dependencies across the company and with external partners, such as cloud and GPU providers.

Compensation

At Atlassian, we strive to design equitable, explainable, and competitive compensation programs. We follow consistent hiring practices and account for each candidate's skills, knowledge, and experience when setting base pay within the range.

Please visit go.atlassian.com/payzones for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

This role may also be eligible for benefits, bonuses, commissions, and equity.

Working knowledge of LLM architecture, inference optimization, serving frameworks and GPU infrastructure economics.
Experience with multi-vendor GPU or inference-provider strategies and AI cost management
Experience with benchmarking and model evaluation methods.
TPMs are not expected to write or read code, but must understand system flows, block architectures and APIs.
A track record of running end-to-end, complex, cross-org technical programs with significant budget.
Strategic thinking and ability to turn business objectives into technical programs with measurable results.
Strong leadership, organizational and communication skills, including influencing senior engineers and executives without direct authority.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager - Core Team Leader
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Sr. Program Manager - Core Team Leader based in the United States.

The Sr. Program Manager - Core Team Leader will lead the execution of multiple strategic product development programs within the medical device industry.

This senior leadership role oversees initiatives across abdominal aortic aneurysm and peripheral vascular product portfolios, ensuring alignment with long-term business objectives and patient needs.

Working closely with Marketing, R&D, Clinical, Quality, Regulatory, Operations, and Commercial teams, you will drive cross-functional collaboration and disciplined program delivery.

You will manage portfolio priorities, budgets, resources, risks, and timelines while ensuring compliance with applicable quality and regulatory requirements.

As a strategic partner to executive and functional leaders, you will guide critical decisions, resolve complex challenges, and support successful product commercialization.

This is an opportunity to influence innovation, develop future program leaders, and contribute to meaningful advancements in vascular care.

The position is fully remote within the United States.

Accountabilities

Responsibilities

As a senior program leader, you will oversee portfolio strategy, cross-functional execution, and product development governance, ensuring programs deliver measurable business value while maintaining a strong focus on patient outcomes. Your responsibilities will include:

Business and Portfolio Leadership
Facilitate product roadmap development, including program selection, prioritization, value alignment, and portfolio optimization.
Establish and manage strategic plan and annual operating plan budgets, timelines, and milestones.
Partner with Marketing, R&D, Clinical, and Commercial leaders to align portfolio priorities with business strategy and evolving market needs.
Coordinate cross-functional efforts to achieve delivery, revenue, and margin commitments.
Promote effective delivery practices, including Design for Reliability and Manufacturability and Voice of the Customer integration.

Program and Execution Leadership
Build and lead high-performing cross-functional Core Teams across multiple concurrent programs.
Drive disciplined program execution through planning, baseline control, and management of scope, schedules, critical paths, costs, resources, risks, and quality.
Represent program strategy and progress to stakeholders and clinicians, communicating both high-level business objectives and technical details.
Act as the primary escalation point for complex issues and trade-off decisions, coordinating timely reviews, approvals, and change control.
Assess the downstream impact of program changes on verification and validation, regulatory submissions, manufacturing, labeling, training, and post-market commitments.
Lead resource planning with functional teams to ensure programs have the appropriate staffing and capabilities.
Coordinate development outputs and commercialization readiness, including manufacturing, supplier, validation, inspection, training, and quality requirements.
Lead product development activities in accordance with applicable design control and product realization requirements, including development planning, design reviews, inputs and outputs, verification, validation, design transfer, and design changes.
Ensure product and process risks are identified, assessed, controlled, escalated, and reviewed throughout the development lifecycle.
Support benefit-risk assessments, quality issue escalations, investigations, corrective actions, and management review activities.
Partner with Quality and Regulatory teams to maintain accurate, complete, and timely development records, including traceability, Design History Files, and other required technical documentation.

Customer and Market Focus
Maintain a strong understanding of global customer needs through collaboration with Marketing, Sales, and external customers.
Keep patient impact and clinical value central to program decisions.
Participate in field activities, regional marketing events, trade shows, and industry seminars to stay informed about customer expectations and market developments.

Talent and Culture Leadership
Mentor and coach Core Team members in partnership with functional leaders, strengthening program management capabilities.
Foster an empowered, collaborative, and decision-oriented culture built on accountability, critical thinking, and continuous improvement.
Contribute to the Innovation Delivery and extended R&D leadership teams, supporting a values-driven approach to organizational leadership.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines extensive program leadership experience with strong business and financial acumen, cross-functional influence, and an understanding of regulated product development environments. The following qualifications are expected:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Science, Business Administration, or a related field.
At least 10 years of experience leading cross-functional, cross-departmental programs, including 7 or more years in advanced management and leadership roles.
Demonstrated success managing complex programs with significant business impact.
Proven experience partnering with Marketing and/or Commercial organizations.
Strong background in program management, strategic planning, and executive-level decision-making.
Experience developing and presenting executive-level business cases and financial models.
Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering Management, or a relevant specialized field preferred.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification highly desirable.
Additional certifications or training in Lean Six Sigma, Agile methodologies, or medical device standards such as ISO 13485 are advantageous.
Medical device industry experience, particularly in new product development and commercialization, preferred.
Familiarity with medical device design controls, risk management, verification and validation, design transfer, clinical research, document and record control, CAPA and nonconformity processes, supplier controls, and global quality and regulatory requirements, including ISO 13485 and FDA QMSR, is an advantage.
Experience developing clinician-focused solutions and leading within diverse, global, matrixed organizations is preferred.
Strong strategic thinking and value orientation, with the ability to translate complex business and market dynamics into clear priorities.
Financial and business acumen, including investment decisions, resource allocation, and operational trade-offs.
Ability to influence without direct authority, build alignment across functions, and navigate competing priorities.
Strong program execution discipline, including risk anticipation, issue resolution, and maintaining momentum across complex initiatives.
Sound judgment and decision-making skills in ambiguous or high-pressure situations.
Commitment to innovation, continuous improvement, and thoughtful risk-taking.
Strong customer and market orientation, with the ability to integrate clinical and customer insights into program decisions.
Excellent leadership, coaching, stakeholder management, and communication skills.
Adaptability and resilience when managing changing priorities in fast-paced environments.

Benefits

Annual base salary of $199,681–$221,675.
Discretionary bonus.
Equity participation, subject to Board of Directors approval, with a four-year vesting schedule.
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and/or Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs).
Generous paid time off, including vacation, sick leave, holidays, and flexible time off for eligible exempt employees.
401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions.
Flexible work arrangements, including remote and hybrid options.
Employee wellness initiatives, mental health resources, and Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
Employee recognition programs and awards.
Commuter benefits or transportation stipends.
Opportunities for career growth and professional development.
The opportunity to contribute to medical innovation and products that support better patient outcomes.

jobs.title: FLEET/JOINT TRAINING PROGRAM MANAGER
jobs.description:
Summary

You will serve as a Fleet/Joint Training Program Manager in the FLT/JOINT TRAINING DIV of COMMANDER US FLEET FORCES COMMAND.

Duties

Help

You will interpret existing Commander, USFFC/Commander, U.S. Pacific Fleet (CPF) policies to support current or planned projects, collaborates with Navy-wide stakeholders to recommend policy revisions for Fleet-wide training requirements.
You will assign goals and objectives to commands geographically dispersed across the globe and routinely interacts with Flag-level senior officers and civilians from all services.
You will provide high-level analytical expertise to address broad Fleet/Joint training requirements included in the Fleet Training Continuum and as directed by the USFFC missions, functions, and tasks.
You will provide leadership in establishing and maintaining effective management processes and a work environment conducive to effective utilization and integration of various resources to include budget, personnel, and equipment.
You will provide expertise and solutions for tactical training range advancements to lead turn advanced threat capabilities and enable the Live Fire with a Purpose program.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

Must be a US Citizen.
Must be determined suitable for federal employment.
Must participate in the direct deposit pay program.
New employees to the Department of the Navy will be required to successfully pass the E-Verify employment verification check. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, visit e-verify.gov
Generally, current federal employees applying for GS jobs must serve at least one year at the next lower grade level. This requirement is called time-in-grade. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.
Within the Department of Defense (DoD), the appointment of retired military members within 180 days immediately following retirement date to a civilian position is subject to the provisions of 5 United States Code 3326.
Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service.
You will be required to obtain and maintain a current valid United States driver’s license.
You will be required to obtain and maintain an interim and/or final security clearance prior to entrance on duty. Failure to obtain and maintain the required level of clearance may result in the withdrawal of a job offer or removal.
Successful completion of a pre-employment drug test (including marijuana) is required. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if you fail to report to the drug test appointment or fail the test. You will be subject to random testing
This position may require travel from normal duty station to CONUS and OCONUS and may include remote or isolated sites. You must be able to travel on military and commercial aircraft for extended periods of time.
You will be required to obtain and maintain a U.S. Passport.
You will be required to complete ethics orientation within three months of appointment and submit a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report, OGE-450, within 30 days of appointment
Supervisors in the executive branch have a heightened personal responsibility for advancing government ethics. You will be required to review the 14 General Principles of Ethical Conduct at 5 CFR 2635.101.

Qualifications

Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-14 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following:

Experience Formulating, Translating, And Aligning Training Policies And Strategic Program Plans With Higher-level National Defense Directives (National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, And CNO Warfighting Concepts) To Prepare Combat Forces Across Multi-domain Environmnents Against Peer And Near Peer Adversaries. Mastery Experience In The Design, Planning, Management, Monitoring, Evaluation, And Assessment Of Complex, Theater-level Navy And Joint Training Programs Throughout All Phases Of The Optimized Fleet Response Plan (OFRP) / Fleet Response Training Plan (FRTP), Ensuring Combat Readiness For Carrier Strike Groups (CSGs), Expeditionary Strike Groups (ESGs), And Surface Action Groups (SAGs). Authoritative Experience Directing Or Executing High-visibility, Enterprise-level Programs, Specifically

Advancing Live, Virtual, and Constructive (LVC) training environments, synthetic training architectures, range advancements (e.g., Live Fire with a Purpose), and modeling and simulation technologies; Providing program leadership, policy direction, or operational oversight for complex weapon systems and strike mission planning portfolios, such as the Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM) program. Demonstrated experience developing international training initiatives and operational frameworks to advance bilateral and allied interoperability, including bilateral accords such as the U.S./UK Statement of Intent regarding aircraft carrier operations, strike integration, and maritime cooperation. Comprehensive experience formulating, justifying, and defending multi-year Program Objective Memorandum (POM) submissions across the Future Years Defense Program (FYDP), performing contract requirement planning, and executing strategic resource allocation for multimillion-dollar training portfolios. Proven experience chairing chartered working groups (e.g., Fleet Training Requirements Management Group, Fleet Training Wholeness Committee), translating complex technical/operational concepts into actionable executive narratives, and negotiating solutions among Flag/General Officers (up to 4-star level), Senior Executive Service (SES) members, OPNAV, Combatant Commands, Type Commanders (TYCOMs), and defense industry executives. Demonstrated executive leadership and supervisory proficiency to direct, mentor, and evaluate a diverse workforce comprising senior federal civilian personnel (GS-14/15), senior military officers (up to O-6), enlisted personnel, and specialized defense technical contractors.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Additional information

This position is covered by the Department of Defense Priority Placement Program.

Additional vacancies may be filled by this announcement.

A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if the selectee fails to meet the pre-employment requirements, including failure to report to any of the scheduled appointments.

Depending on the hiring organization and the position being filled, job requirements (e.g., security clearance, travel, drug testing, financial disclosure filing, bargaining unit status, etc.) may vary. Other hiring managers filling similar positions may offer relocation expense reimbursement and/or may offer recruitment incentives for new employees, depending on funding availability and in accordance with policy. If you opt-in and are referred on a certificate, your resume will be available to other hiring managers for 180-days from the date the job announcement closes. Opting in does not impact your application for this announcement, nor does it guarantee further consideration for additional positions.

Federal annuitant information: The selection of an annuitant is subject to the Department of Defense and Department of the Navy policy on the employment of annuitants. Policy information may be found at: http://www.secnav.navy.mil/donhr/Documents/CivilianJobs/FedCivAnnuitants.pdf

ICTAP Applicants:

ICTAP candidates must provide copies of all of the following documentation at the time of application: 1) agency notice; 2) most recent performance appraisal; and 3) most recent SF-50 or notification of personnel action that includes position, grade level, and duty location. This position is subject to work an uncommon tour, including nights, weekends, and holidays to meet mission requirements. Overtime or night differential pay and/or unusual duty hours may be required.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Cybersecurity & Privacy (O-5 Billet) Non-Supervisory
jobs.description:
Summary

IHSC seeks a USPHS O-5 Cybersecurity & Privacy Program Manager to lead a portfolio of health IT cybersecurity and privacy compliance work. The incumbent will coordinate Risk Management Framework and privacy activities, acquisition requirements, schedules, and stakeholders across IHSC. This non-supervisory position requires strong program management, communication, and Federal compliance coordination skills.

This position is only open to USPHS officers and Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidates

Duties

Duties And Responsibilities

Leads an assigned portfolio of cybersecurity and privacy compliance projects, systems, acquisitions, and workstreams. Serves as the primary point of accountability for coordination, progress monitoring, and issue identification within the assigned portfolio.
Develops and maintains milestone schedules for assigned projects and workstreams. Tracks project status, dependencies, constraints, deliverables, and schedule risks; identifies potential slippage early enough to support intervention and resolution.
Supports authorization activities for assigned systems, including coordination and tracking of Risk Management Framework (RMF) documentation, security artifacts, plans of action and milestones, evidence, and related authorization packages.
Coordinates with System Owners, Authorizing Officials, Federal Information System Security Officers, Office of the Chief Information Officer cybersecurity authorities, privacy officials, acquisition personnel, contracting personnel, and contractor support staff to ensure required input is obtained, considered, documented, and acted upon.
Identifies cybersecurity and privacy implications early in project and acquisition planning. Coordinates privacy reviews and tracks formal privacy determinations, assessments, and resulting actions from the appropriate privacy officials.
Works with the Acquisition Planning Office and other stakeholders to identify and incorporate cybersecurity and privacy requirements into acquisition planning, requirements documentation, statements of work, performance work statements, and related acquisition artifacts before referral to contracting.
Ensures cybersecurity and privacy requirements identified during planning are carried forward through contract performance, oversight, system implementation, and lifecycle management.
Coordinates contractor-provided cybersecurity support through appropriate Government channels. Preserves Government decision-making authority and does not issue formal direction to contractor personnel unless separately authorized.
Identifies, assesses, documents, and escalates cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, and schedule risks within the assigned portfolio. Provides recommendations and clearly explains potential programmatic, cost, schedule, operational, and mission impacts.
Coordinates with the Portfolio Management Office to ensure assigned milestones, dependencies, constraints, risks, and resource considerations are accurately reflected in enterprise schedules, planning activities, and portfolio reporting.
Maintains complete, retrievable, accurate, and protected compliance records that are traceable to the decisions, determinations, and actions they support.
Develops status reports, briefings, dashboards, correspondence, and other written products for the CCO Supervisory Lead and relevant stakeholders. Communicates technical and compliance issues in clear, concise, programmatically relevant terms.
Participates in meetings, working groups, acquisition planning sessions, and program reviews as a cybersecurity and privacy compliance coordination representative for assigned work.
Remains flexible and able to adapt to changing priorities, schedules, work requirements, and mission needs.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

You must be a U.S. citizen to apply for this position.
You must successfully pass a background investigation.
You must successfully pass a drug screen.
Males born after 12/31/59 must certify registration with Selective Service.
Requirements by Closing Date: Unless otherwise noted, you must meet all requirements by the closing date of the announcement.
Service Remaining Requirement Agreement: Upon appointment to this position, officers will be required to serve an 18 to 24-month commitment to IHSC.
ASSIGNMENT PAY AGREEMENT: You must not have a current Assignment Pay Agreement. However, if you have a current Assignment Pay Agreement, it must be fulfilled within 90 days of your application submission.
Applicants must be a current USPHS Commissioned Corps Officer or USPHS Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidate.

Civilians are not eligible for this position.

Applicants without a USPHS commission must begin the USPHS Commissioned Corps application process before applying to this position. Applicants must review the USPHS application requirements and submit an application at www.usphs.gov/apply-now/.
Continued employment is contingent upon appointment to, and maintenance of, active-duty status in the USPHS Commissioned Corps.
PHS officers must participate in IHSC TDY On-Call Schedule (ITOS.) ITOS is either an entire month or two 16-day periods a year where, depending on the needs of the agency, the officer is required to be available to serve.

Qualifications

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Sitting and/or standing for extended periods of time, generally six to eight hours.
Performing repeated bending motions as needed.
Average manual dexterity for computer operation and handling routine office equipment.
Telephone and virtual meeting participation for extended periods.
Occasional travel may be required in support of CAMS, HITU, IHSC, and unit mission requirements.

Education

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Qualifying degree from the U.S. Public Health Service officer's category and progressively responsible professional experience relevant to the officer's category.
At least two years of meaningful experience in one or more of the following areas:
Cybersecurity, information security, information assurance, or Federal information technology governance;
Privacy, information governance, compliance, or risk management;
Risk Management Framework, authorization support, or continuous monitoring;
Program management, project management, contractor management, health information technology, or healthcare technology.
Ability to manage assigned projects and portfolios where technical work is performed by specialists whom the incumbent does not supervise.
Working knowledge of Federal cybersecurity and privacy compliance practices, including authorization activities, RMF concepts, continuous monitoring, privacy reviews, and compliance documentation, sufficient to manage work and recognize risk.
Ability to understand technical discussions, ask informed questions, analyze information, and translate technical findings into schedule, cost, mission, operational, and programmatic impacts.
Knowledge of the Federal acquisition lifecycle sufficient to ensure cybersecurity and privacy requirements are incorporated into acquisitions during planning and remain addressed through contract performance and oversight.
Ability to manage multiple workstreams concurrently at varying stages of planning, acquisition, implementation, authorization, and operations while maintaining accurate milestones, dependencies, status information, and records.
Ability to coordinate contractor-provided technical support while preserving Government decision-making authority and complying with applicable acquisition and contracting requirements.
Ability to exercise sound judgment, initiative, independence, and follow-through when managing sensitive, complex, and multidisciplinary programmatic issues.
Ability to identify, assess, document, and communicate risks and provide actionable recommendations to supervisors and stakeholders.
Ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and professionally in writing and orally, including through status reports, briefings, meeting facilitation, and formal correspondence.
Knowledge and skill in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and project-tracking tools.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with Federal personnel, contractors, technical specialists, acquisition personnel, privacy officials, and executive stakeholders.
Relevant coursework, professional training, or certifications may strengthen an applicant's preparation. Examples include Security+, Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified in Governance, Risk and Compliance (CGRC), privacy credentials, Federal Acquisition Certification for Contracting Officer's Representatives (FAC-COR), or comparable credentials. Such credentials are valuable but not independently required.
Must be able to attain and maintain the background investigation and suitability determination required for the position.
Must maintain professional licensure or certification applicable to the officer's discipline, if applicable.
Must be able to travel in support of unit mission requirements.

Additional Information

This position is located within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), and the Office of Deputy Assistant Director (DAD) of Administration, Health Information and Technology Unit (HITU).

IHSC has a multi-sector, multidisciplinary workforce of more than 1600 employees, including U.S. Public Health Service (PHS) commissioned officers, federal civil servants, and contract staff. The IHSC provides on-site direct patient care to ICE detainees at 17 detention facilities throughout the country and manages the provision of off-site medical care for detainees housed in approximately 128 additional Intergovernmental Service Agreement (IGSA) facilities. The ICE detainee population is approximately 45,000 detainees daily, with an average length of stay of approximately 30 days, and over 400,000 detainees annually. The IHSC also provides medical support during ICE enforcement operations in the air, on the ground, and at sea.

The Health Information and Technology Unit (HITU) is responsible for managing the acquisition lifecycle of IHSC IT contracts in partnership with the Office of Acquisition Management and the Office of the Chief Information Officer.

The IHSC IT Contracts and Acquisition Management Section (CAMS) provides dedicated ownership of pre-award acquisition planning, post-award contract governance, and cybersecurity and privacy compliance coordination across the acquisition and contract lifecycle for medical assets. In addition, working with partners across ICE, CAMS works to ensure all equipment meets security requirements.

Supervisory Controls

The Cybersecurity & Privacy Program Manager works under the general supervision of the Cybersecurity Compliance Office Supervisory Lead.

The incumbent plans, organizes, and carries out assigned portfolio responsibilities; determines the sequence of work; develops methods for tracking and coordinating compliance activities; and seeks supervisory guidance on matters involving policy, resource decisions, significant risk, conflicts, or issues requiring escalation outside the office.

Assignments may be long-term, recurring, or broadly defined. Work is reviewed for alignment with office standards, feasibility, compatibility with other work, completeness of documentation, effectiveness in meeting requirements, and achievement of expected results.

The incumbent manages the assigned portfolio and provides recommendations but does not self-assign work or escalate matters outside the office without coordination with the CCO Supervisory Lead.

Lead critical ICT project as part of TZV’s Next Generation CAD Transformation Program

Full-time | 18 months fixed term | Burwood East | 160,518 base + 12% superannuation

About Triple Zero Victoria

Triple Zero Victoria (TZV) provides the critical link between the Victorian community and the state’s emergency services agencies. It provides Victoria’s 24-hour emergency call-taking and dispatch services for Police, Fire, Ambulance and VICSES.

This integration of emergency services communications within Triple Zero Victoria is unique in Australia and rare worldwide. The team at Triple Zero Victoria are deeply committed to the community they serve and are among the most dedicated and highly skilled in their field.

About The Role

The On Call Integration Project forms part of the Cardinal Program and is responsible for delivering critical system and data integration between Next Generation OnCall CAD system and Emergency Service Organisation (ESO) dispatch systems. The Senior Project Manager is a key leadership role within the Cardinal Program team responsible for delivering this key Project within the agreed timeline, scope and multi-million-dollar budget.

Day To Day Responsibilities Include

Develop and maintain all core project documentation—including Project Management Plans, budgets, schedules, status reports, and key controls (risk, issue, variation, and lessons learned logs)—in accordance with TZV’s framework.
Establish and maintain robust project governance and reporting aligned with the Project Management Framework to drive oversight and decision-making.
Plan project resource requirements and lead a cross-functional matrix team of Solution Architects, Business Analysts, Developers, and QA Engineers to drive end-to-end delivery from design through validation.
Lead Change Management and Communication Plans to drive seamless adoption and keep internal and external stakeholders continuously informed
Coordinate internal cross-functional teams (IT, Legal, Procurement), external vendor/consultant partners, and external stakeholders (ESOs) to deliver all project objectives collaboratively

About You

The successful candidate will have the following experience, skills and attributes:

Tertiary qualification in Project Management and/or recognised certification in project delivery methodologies (e.g., PRINCE2, PMBOK, SAFe, Scrum, or equivalent).
Extensive project management experience in large technology projects.
Demonstrated ability to successfully implement, coordinate and deliver projects with multiple users over multiple sites.
Strong interpersonal skills, a hands-on approach and the ability to work collaboratively at all levels of the organisation.
Strong negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills and ability to influence others to obtain support and work toward a common goal.
Experience with Agile delivery methodologies is highly desirable.

Executive and Senior Leadership are committed to empowering employees towards their professional and personal goals. Clarity of vision provided by a long-term ICT Strategy will enable clear role descriptions, variety of work and pathways for growth. With substantial transformation currently underway and more to come, you will have the chance to bring your eclectic experiences to shape the delivery models. The sector-wide remit, defined by a heavily integrated eco-system of technologies, whilst challenging, will present the opportunity to develop high quality networks and hone your craft in a fast-moving set up where high availability is paramount, facets that hold you in good stead for the future.

Employee assistance program for employees and eligible family members
Discounted health insurance, banking services and gym membership
‘Memberlink’ discount card, accepted by 1,000's of retailers and services providers

jobs.description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:

At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.

In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence

About The Role

The California State Controller’s Office (SCO) is currently implementing a large and complex SaaS solution to support the California State Payroll System (CSPS) project. CSPS is a massive project, and the implementation includes both Personnel and Payroll functionality to support the needs of some 300,000 employees across 160 agencies and 21 bargaining units. With an estimated project budget exceeding $1 billion and staffing approaching 200 IT professionals, this highly complex effort is expected to continue for the next several years.

Description

The Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for execution, maintenance and enhancement of the CSPS Project Management Plans.

PMO responsibilities include:

ensuring that formal PM processes are in place and followed across all project workstreams (leadership, functional, technical, and organizational change management)
ensuring documentation is maintained in accordance with policy and procedure
regular periodic reporting on project risks, issues, and overall health, including stakeholder presentations as needed
assisting the CSPS Leadership Team in monitoring system integrator performance
providing analysis and recommendations for improvements to project management processes

The CSPS PMO is currently staffed by four senior project managers who each work directly with a state and system integrator counterpart.

Contract Required Qualifications For The Senior Project Manager Role

Requires a minimum of seven (7) years of broad, extensive and increasingly responsible experience applying PM principles, methods, techniques, and tools. At least four (4) years of that experience must have been as a senior PM of one or more large or complex IT projects.

Possession of (a) a bachelor’s degree, and (b) a valid Project Management Professional (PMP) certification from the Project Management Institute (PMI)

Additional qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis. The PMP certification is required and may not be substituted with additional experience.

Additional Qualifications

The Senior PM role requires proven project management skills in a highly complex and large-scale IT implementation. The successful candidate will need to work well in a dynamic environment, providing exceptional client service with outstanding professionalism. The role requires direct interaction with client and system integrator staff, as well as:

Strong analytical, organizational and core project management skills
Ability to help client personnel to leverage technology to solve business problems
Strong verbal and written communication skills with a commitment to client service and professionalism
Possess conceptual thinking skills, creativity and flexibility
Work well both independently and in a team
Must be self-sufficient and have the ability to self-manage
Experienced and comfortable in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio)
Ability to learn quickly and adapt with other technology applications in day-to-day work

Other

Candidates will need to complete and pass a background check conducted by SCO prior to beginning work
Remote work is allowed, but staff must be based in the continental United States. With advance notice, project staff will occasionally need to travel to Sacramento for project meetings.
Normal working hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific time. All staff, regardless of location, are required to perform duties within those hours.

We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Crowe, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,400.00 - $205,300.00 per year.

Our Benefits:

Your exceptional people experience starts here. At Crowe, we know that great people are what makes a great firm. We care about our people and offer employees a comprehensive total rewards package. Learn more about what working at Crowe can mean for you!

How You Can Grow:

We will nurture your talent in an inclusive culture that values diversity. You will have the chance to meet on a consistent basis with your Career Coach that will guide you in your career goals and aspirations. Learn more about where talent can prosper!

More about Crowe:

Crowe provides professional services through two separate entities: Crowe LLP delivers audit and attest services, and Crowe Advisory LLC provides tax, advisory, consulting, and other nonattest services.

The Crowe Global network consists of more than 300 independent accounting and advisory services firms in more than 150 countries around the globe, making it one of the largest accounting networks in the world*. As independent members of Crowe Global, Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC serve clients worldwide. (*As of July 2026)

Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC (and their respective subsidiary entities) provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetics, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC (and their respective subsidiary entities) does not accept unsolicited candidates, referrals or resumes from any staffing agency, recruiting service, sourcing entity or any other third-party paid service at any time. Any referrals, resumes or candidates submitted to Crowe, or any employee or owner of Crowe without a pre-existing agreement signed by both parties covering the submission will be considered the property of Crowe, and free of charge.

Crowe will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act.

Please visit our webpage to see notices of the various state and local Ban-the-Box laws and Fair Chance Ordinances, where applicable.
