Summary

You will serve as a Fleet/Joint Training Program Manager in the FLT/JOINT TRAINING DIV of COMMANDER US FLEET FORCES COMMAND.

Duties

Help

You will interpret existing Commander, USFFC/Commander, U.S. Pacific Fleet (CPF) policies to support current or planned projects, collaborates with Navy-wide stakeholders to recommend policy revisions for Fleet-wide training requirements.
You will assign goals and objectives to commands geographically dispersed across the globe and routinely interacts with Flag-level senior officers and civilians from all services.
You will provide high-level analytical expertise to address broad Fleet/Joint training requirements included in the Fleet Training Continuum and as directed by the USFFC missions, functions, and tasks.
You will provide leadership in establishing and maintaining effective management processes and a work environment conducive to effective utilization and integration of various resources to include budget, personnel, and equipment.
You will provide expertise and solutions for tactical training range advancements to lead turn advanced threat capabilities and enable the Live Fire with a Purpose program.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

Must be a US Citizen.
Must be determined suitable for federal employment.
Must participate in the direct deposit pay program.
New employees to the Department of the Navy will be required to successfully pass the E-Verify employment verification check. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, visit e-verify.gov
Generally, current federal employees applying for GS jobs must serve at least one year at the next lower grade level. This requirement is called time-in-grade. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.
Within the Department of Defense (DoD), the appointment of retired military members within 180 days immediately following retirement date to a civilian position is subject to the provisions of 5 United States Code 3326.
Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service.
You will be required to obtain and maintain a current valid United States driver’s license.
You will be required to obtain and maintain an interim and/or final security clearance prior to entrance on duty. Failure to obtain and maintain the required level of clearance may result in the withdrawal of a job offer or removal.
Successful completion of a pre-employment drug test (including marijuana) is required. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if you fail to report to the drug test appointment or fail the test. You will be subject to random testing
This position may require travel from normal duty station to CONUS and OCONUS and may include remote or isolated sites. You must be able to travel on military and commercial aircraft for extended periods of time.
You will be required to obtain and maintain a U.S. Passport.
You will be required to complete ethics orientation within three months of appointment and submit a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report, OGE-450, within 30 days of appointment
Supervisors in the executive branch have a heightened personal responsibility for advancing government ethics. You will be required to review the 14 General Principles of Ethical Conduct at 5 CFR 2635.101.

Qualifications

Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-14 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following:

Experience Formulating, Translating, And Aligning Training Policies And Strategic Program Plans With Higher-level National Defense Directives (National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, And CNO Warfighting Concepts) To Prepare Combat Forces Across Multi-domain Environmnents Against Peer And Near Peer Adversaries. Mastery Experience In The Design, Planning, Management, Monitoring, Evaluation, And Assessment Of Complex, Theater-level Navy And Joint Training Programs Throughout All Phases Of The Optimized Fleet Response Plan (OFRP) / Fleet Response Training Plan (FRTP), Ensuring Combat Readiness For Carrier Strike Groups (CSGs), Expeditionary Strike Groups (ESGs), And Surface Action Groups (SAGs). Authoritative Experience Directing Or Executing High-visibility, Enterprise-level Programs, Specifically

Advancing Live, Virtual, and Constructive (LVC) training environments, synthetic training architectures, range advancements (e.g., Live Fire with a Purpose), and modeling and simulation technologies; Providing program leadership, policy direction, or operational oversight for complex weapon systems and strike mission planning portfolios, such as the Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM) program. Demonstrated experience developing international training initiatives and operational frameworks to advance bilateral and allied interoperability, including bilateral accords such as the U.S./UK Statement of Intent regarding aircraft carrier operations, strike integration, and maritime cooperation. Comprehensive experience formulating, justifying, and defending multi-year Program Objective Memorandum (POM) submissions across the Future Years Defense Program (FYDP), performing contract requirement planning, and executing strategic resource allocation for multimillion-dollar training portfolios. Proven experience chairing chartered working groups (e.g., Fleet Training Requirements Management Group, Fleet Training Wholeness Committee), translating complex technical/operational concepts into actionable executive narratives, and negotiating solutions among Flag/General Officers (up to 4-star level), Senior Executive Service (SES) members, OPNAV, Combatant Commands, Type Commanders (TYCOMs), and defense industry executives. Demonstrated executive leadership and supervisory proficiency to direct, mentor, and evaluate a diverse workforce comprising senior federal civilian personnel (GS-14/15), senior military officers (up to O-6), enlisted personnel, and specialized defense technical contractors.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Cybersecurity & Privacy (O-5 Billet) Non-Supervisory
new_jobs.description:
Summary

IHSC seeks a USPHS O-5 Cybersecurity & Privacy Program Manager to lead a portfolio of health IT cybersecurity and privacy compliance work. The incumbent will coordinate Risk Management Framework and privacy activities, acquisition requirements, schedules, and stakeholders across IHSC. This non-supervisory position requires strong program management, communication, and Federal compliance coordination skills.

This position is only open to USPHS officers and Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidates

Duties

Duties And Responsibilities

Leads an assigned portfolio of cybersecurity and privacy compliance projects, systems, acquisitions, and workstreams. Serves as the primary point of accountability for coordination, progress monitoring, and issue identification within the assigned portfolio.
Develops and maintains milestone schedules for assigned projects and workstreams. Tracks project status, dependencies, constraints, deliverables, and schedule risks; identifies potential slippage early enough to support intervention and resolution.
Supports authorization activities for assigned systems, including coordination and tracking of Risk Management Framework (RMF) documentation, security artifacts, plans of action and milestones, evidence, and related authorization packages.
Coordinates with System Owners, Authorizing Officials, Federal Information System Security Officers, Office of the Chief Information Officer cybersecurity authorities, privacy officials, acquisition personnel, contracting personnel, and contractor support staff to ensure required input is obtained, considered, documented, and acted upon.
Identifies cybersecurity and privacy implications early in project and acquisition planning. Coordinates privacy reviews and tracks formal privacy determinations, assessments, and resulting actions from the appropriate privacy officials.
Works with the Acquisition Planning Office and other stakeholders to identify and incorporate cybersecurity and privacy requirements into acquisition planning, requirements documentation, statements of work, performance work statements, and related acquisition artifacts before referral to contracting.
Ensures cybersecurity and privacy requirements identified during planning are carried forward through contract performance, oversight, system implementation, and lifecycle management.
Coordinates contractor-provided cybersecurity support through appropriate Government channels. Preserves Government decision-making authority and does not issue formal direction to contractor personnel unless separately authorized.
Identifies, assesses, documents, and escalates cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, and schedule risks within the assigned portfolio. Provides recommendations and clearly explains potential programmatic, cost, schedule, operational, and mission impacts.
Coordinates with the Portfolio Management Office to ensure assigned milestones, dependencies, constraints, risks, and resource considerations are accurately reflected in enterprise schedules, planning activities, and portfolio reporting.
Maintains complete, retrievable, accurate, and protected compliance records that are traceable to the decisions, determinations, and actions they support.
Develops status reports, briefings, dashboards, correspondence, and other written products for the CCO Supervisory Lead and relevant stakeholders. Communicates technical and compliance issues in clear, concise, programmatically relevant terms.
Participates in meetings, working groups, acquisition planning sessions, and program reviews as a cybersecurity and privacy compliance coordination representative for assigned work.
Remains flexible and able to adapt to changing priorities, schedules, work requirements, and mission needs.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

You must be a U.S. citizen to apply for this position.
You must successfully pass a background investigation.
You must successfully pass a drug screen.
Males born after 12/31/59 must certify registration with Selective Service.
Requirements by Closing Date: Unless otherwise noted, you must meet all requirements by the closing date of the announcement.
Service Remaining Requirement Agreement: Upon appointment to this position, officers will be required to serve an 18 to 24-month commitment to IHSC.
ASSIGNMENT PAY AGREEMENT: You must not have a current Assignment Pay Agreement. However, if you have a current Assignment Pay Agreement, it must be fulfilled within 90 days of your application submission.
Applicants must be a current USPHS Commissioned Corps Officer or USPHS Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidate.

Civilians are not eligible for this position.

Applicants without a USPHS commission must begin the USPHS Commissioned Corps application process before applying to this position. Applicants must review the USPHS application requirements and submit an application at www.usphs.gov/apply-now/.
Continued employment is contingent upon appointment to, and maintenance of, active-duty status in the USPHS Commissioned Corps.
PHS officers must participate in IHSC TDY On-Call Schedule (ITOS.) ITOS is either an entire month or two 16-day periods a year where, depending on the needs of the agency, the officer is required to be available to serve.

Qualifications

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Sitting and/or standing for extended periods of time, generally six to eight hours.
Performing repeated bending motions as needed.
Average manual dexterity for computer operation and handling routine office equipment.
Telephone and virtual meeting participation for extended periods.
Occasional travel may be required in support of CAMS, HITU, IHSC, and unit mission requirements.

Education

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Qualifying degree from the U.S. Public Health Service officer's category and progressively responsible professional experience relevant to the officer's category.
At least two years of meaningful experience in one or more of the following areas:
Cybersecurity, information security, information assurance, or Federal information technology governance;
Privacy, information governance, compliance, or risk management;
Risk Management Framework, authorization support, or continuous monitoring;
Program management, project management, contractor management, health information technology, or healthcare technology.
Ability to manage assigned projects and portfolios where technical work is performed by specialists whom the incumbent does not supervise.
Working knowledge of Federal cybersecurity and privacy compliance practices, including authorization activities, RMF concepts, continuous monitoring, privacy reviews, and compliance documentation, sufficient to manage work and recognize risk.
Ability to understand technical discussions, ask informed questions, analyze information, and translate technical findings into schedule, cost, mission, operational, and programmatic impacts.
Knowledge of the Federal acquisition lifecycle sufficient to ensure cybersecurity and privacy requirements are incorporated into acquisitions during planning and remain addressed through contract performance and oversight.
Ability to manage multiple workstreams concurrently at varying stages of planning, acquisition, implementation, authorization, and operations while maintaining accurate milestones, dependencies, status information, and records.
Ability to coordinate contractor-provided technical support while preserving Government decision-making authority and complying with applicable acquisition and contracting requirements.
Ability to exercise sound judgment, initiative, independence, and follow-through when managing sensitive, complex, and multidisciplinary programmatic issues.
Ability to identify, assess, document, and communicate risks and provide actionable recommendations to supervisors and stakeholders.
Ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and professionally in writing and orally, including through status reports, briefings, meeting facilitation, and formal correspondence.
Knowledge and skill in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and project-tracking tools.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with Federal personnel, contractors, technical specialists, acquisition personnel, privacy officials, and executive stakeholders.
Relevant coursework, professional training, or certifications may strengthen an applicant's preparation. Examples include Security+, Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified in Governance, Risk and Compliance (CGRC), privacy credentials, Federal Acquisition Certification for Contracting Officer's Representatives (FAC-COR), or comparable credentials. Such credentials are valuable but not independently required.
Must be able to attain and maintain the background investigation and suitability determination required for the position.
Must maintain professional licensure or certification applicable to the officer's discipline, if applicable.
Must be able to travel in support of unit mission requirements.

Additional Information

This position is located within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), and the Office of Deputy Assistant Director (DAD) of Administration, Health Information and Technology Unit (HITU).

IHSC has a multi-sector, multidisciplinary workforce of more than 1600 employees, including U.S. Public Health Service (PHS) commissioned officers, federal civil servants, and contract staff. The IHSC provides on-site direct patient care to ICE detainees at 17 detention facilities throughout the country and manages the provision of off-site medical care for detainees housed in approximately 128 additional Intergovernmental Service Agreement (IGSA) facilities. The ICE detainee population is approximately 45,000 detainees daily, with an average length of stay of approximately 30 days, and over 400,000 detainees annually. The IHSC also provides medical support during ICE enforcement operations in the air, on the ground, and at sea.

The Health Information and Technology Unit (HITU) is responsible for managing the acquisition lifecycle of IHSC IT contracts in partnership with the Office of Acquisition Management and the Office of the Chief Information Officer.

The IHSC IT Contracts and Acquisition Management Section (CAMS) provides dedicated ownership of pre-award acquisition planning, post-award contract governance, and cybersecurity and privacy compliance coordination across the acquisition and contract lifecycle for medical assets. In addition, working with partners across ICE, CAMS works to ensure all equipment meets security requirements.

Supervisory Controls

The Cybersecurity & Privacy Program Manager works under the general supervision of the Cybersecurity Compliance Office Supervisory Lead.

The incumbent plans, organizes, and carries out assigned portfolio responsibilities; determines the sequence of work; develops methods for tracking and coordinating compliance activities; and seeks supervisory guidance on matters involving policy, resource decisions, significant risk, conflicts, or issues requiring escalation outside the office.

Assignments may be long-term, recurring, or broadly defined. Work is reviewed for alignment with office standards, feasibility, compatibility with other work, completeness of documentation, effectiveness in meeting requirements, and achievement of expected results.

The incumbent manages the assigned portfolio and provides recommendations but does not self-assign work or escalate matters outside the office without coordination with the CCO Supervisory Lead.

JOB DESCRIPTION: Project Manager – AI

Enterprise Technology & Digital Transformation Lifecycle

Strategic Objective

The AI-PM is a strategic, execution-focused leader driving the company's AI transformation journey. This individual bridges the gap between business leadership, technical teams, and external vendors to deploy company-wide automation, save time, reduce costs, and dramatically improve organizational output quality.

Key Success Metrics

Processing & Time Savings:
Measurable reduction in manual processing time per department and total corporate hours saved.
Financial Impact:
Positive, systematically tracked ROI achieved within defined product and project timelines.
Adoption & Velocity:
High active adoption rates of automated tools across business units and consistent quarterly AI deployments.
Quality & Satisfaction:
Improved pre- vs. post-implementation quality parameters and verified employee satisfaction indexes.

2. Core Responsibilities

AI Strategy & Roadmap Development

High-Impact Strategy:
Define and execute a phased, high-impact AI roadmap aligned with overarching business objectives across Finance, HR, Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Support.
Prioritization:
Assess and prioritize technical initiatives based on operational feasibility, pipeline impact, and financial ROI potential.
Market Awareness:
Monitor global technology shifts, benchmark competitor ecosystems, and deliver a quarterly 'State of AI' landscape report to the executive leadership team.

Workflow Automation & Platform Architecture

System Integration:
Design and oversee end-to-end automation workflows that integrate smoothly with existing enterprise applications (CRM, HRMS, Legacy Databases, etc.).
Platform Mastery:
Demonstrate strong hands-on mastery of modern enterprise workflow tools such as n8n, Make, Zapier, or Microsoft Power Automate.
Governance & Compliance:
Establish robust AI governance, data privacy parameters, continuous model-monitoring controls, and ethical compliance frameworks from day one.
Build vs. Buy Analysis:
Evaluate complex commercial build vs. buy solutions with structured technical and financial risk analysis.

Vibe Coding, Prototyping & Technical Translation

Rapid Prototyping:
Utilize 'vibe coding' principles using natural language inside AI development shells (Cursor, Replit AI, GitHub Copilot, v0) to accelerate prototype deployment without engineering bottlenecks.
Discovery Engineering:
Lead discovery workshops with business heads to translate practical pain points into crisp system requirements, user stories, and precise technical briefs.
Quality Assurance Check:
Evaluate early low-code/vibe-coded prototypes for production readiness before passing them to core developer lines.

ROI Analytics & Financial Case Development

Financial Modeling:
Build data-grounded financial models projecting cost optimizations, capacity release, and structural quality returns to capture leadership approval.
KPI Dashboards:
Monitor and distribute detailed monthly dashboards reporting target vs. actual ROI performance benchmarks.

Vendor, Client & Management Communication

Vendor Optimization:
Serve as the master point of contact for external AI software companies, SaaS vendors, and specialized system integrators; negotiate precise SLAs.
Executive Advisory:
Translate complex, multi-layered algorithmic and machine learning engineering terms into simplified, accessible strategic vocabulary for non-technical stakeholders.
Culture Catalyst:
Champion a data-driven, AI-first work culture through internal continuous learning series, lunch-and-learn presentations, and proactive change management strategies.

Engineering Oversight & Architecture (Added Advantage)

Velocity Protection:
Partner directly with engineering lines, data scientists, and DevOps specialists to break execution blockers and maintain delivery timeline momentum.
Technical Foundation:
Maintain a functional, operational literacy in database structures (MySQL, PostgreSQL, NoSQL architectures) and foundational programming frameworks (Python, JavaScript, REST APIs, JSON data maps) to effectively guide core product decisions.

Team Leadership & Personnel Management

Cross-Functional Operations:
Directly coordinate, mentor, and track performance across a cross-functional Agile unit comprising developers, data analysts, system architects, UI/UX engineers, and QA assets.
Psychological Safety:
Construct a highly collaborative, innovative, and safe team environment that incentivizes experimentation, speed, and learning from failure.
Resource Optimization:
Control tactical resource allocation patterns to avoid personnel burnout while defending roadmap velocity commitments.

3. Qualifications & Competencies

Required Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor's or Master's university degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a heavily analytical engineering field.
Professional Background:
5–9 years of structural project management experience, with a validated minimum of 3 years strictly dedicated to AI deployment, complex workflow automation, or enterprise-scale digital transformations.
Delivery Execution:
Proven, end-to-end portfolio tracking product evolution from conceptual design phase through to live enterprise rollout using Agile, Scrum, or hybrid workflow methods.
Integration Literacy:
Verifiable hands-on track record using cloud workflow orchestration engines (n8n, Make, Zapier, or Power Automate).
Commercial Competence:
Documented background creating financial case summaries, tracking cost-mitigation parameters, and proving tech investments ROI.

We operate in an aggressive, progressive corporate landscape where internal workflow automation and AI scaling are resourced as primary, non-negotiable competitive business advantages.

Lead critical ICT project as part of TZV’s Next Generation CAD Transformation Program
Work as part of a high performing team and engage with stakeholders across TZV and Victoria’s emergency services sector
Full-time | 18 months fixed term | Burwood East | 160,518 base + 12% superannuation

About Triple Zero Victoria

Triple Zero Victoria (TZV) provides the critical link between the Victorian community and the state’s emergency services agencies. It provides Victoria’s 24-hour emergency call-taking and dispatch services for Police, Fire, Ambulance and VICSES.

This integration of emergency services communications within Triple Zero Victoria is unique in Australia and rare worldwide. The team at Triple Zero Victoria are deeply committed to the community they serve and are among the most dedicated and highly skilled in their field.

About The Role

The On Call Integration Project forms part of the Cardinal Program and is responsible for delivering critical system and data integration between Next Generation OnCall CAD system and Emergency Service Organisation (ESO) dispatch systems. The Senior Project Manager is a key leadership role within the Cardinal Program team responsible for delivering this key Project within the agreed timeline, scope and multi-million-dollar budget.

Day To Day Responsibilities Include

Develop and maintain all core project documentation—including Project Management Plans, budgets, schedules, status reports, and key controls (risk, issue, variation, and lessons learned logs)—in accordance with TZV’s framework.
Establish and maintain robust project governance and reporting aligned with the Project Management Framework to drive oversight and decision-making.
Plan project resource requirements and lead a cross-functional matrix team of Solution Architects, Business Analysts, Developers, and QA Engineers to drive end-to-end delivery from design through validation.
Lead Change Management and Communication Plans to drive seamless adoption and keep internal and external stakeholders continuously informed
Coordinate internal cross-functional teams (IT, Legal, Procurement), external vendor/consultant partners, and external stakeholders (ESOs) to deliver all project objectives collaboratively

About You

The successful candidate will have the following experience, skills and attributes:

Tertiary qualification in Project Management and/or recognised certification in project delivery methodologies (e.g., PRINCE2, PMBOK, SAFe, Scrum, or equivalent).
Extensive project management experience in large technology projects.
Demonstrated ability to successfully implement, coordinate and deliver projects with multiple users over multiple sites.
Strong interpersonal skills, a hands-on approach and the ability to work collaboratively at all levels of the organisation.
Strong negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills and ability to influence others to obtain support and work toward a common goal.
Experience with Agile delivery methodologies is highly desirable.

Executive and Senior Leadership are committed to empowering employees towards their professional and personal goals. Clarity of vision provided by a long-term ICT Strategy will enable clear role descriptions, variety of work and pathways for growth. With substantial transformation currently underway and more to come, you will have the chance to bring your eclectic experiences to shape the delivery models. The sector-wide remit, defined by a heavily integrated eco-system of technologies, whilst challenging, will present the opportunity to develop high quality networks and hone your craft in a fast-moving set up where high availability is paramount, facets that hold you in good stead for the future.

Employee assistance program for employees and eligible family members
Discounted health insurance, banking services and gym membership

As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence

About The Role

The California State Controller’s Office (SCO) is currently implementing a large and complex SaaS solution to support the California State Payroll System (CSPS) project. CSPS is a massive project, and the implementation includes both Personnel and Payroll functionality to support the needs of some 300,000 employees across 160 agencies and 21 bargaining units. With an estimated project budget exceeding $1 billion and staffing approaching 200 IT professionals, this highly complex effort is expected to continue for the next several years.

Description

The Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for execution, maintenance and enhancement of the CSPS Project Management Plans.

PMO responsibilities include:

ensuring that formal PM processes are in place and followed across all project workstreams (leadership, functional, technical, and organizational change management)
ensuring documentation is maintained in accordance with policy and procedure
regular periodic reporting on project risks, issues, and overall health, including stakeholder presentations as needed
assisting the CSPS Leadership Team in monitoring system integrator performance
providing analysis and recommendations for improvements to project management processes

The CSPS PMO is currently staffed by four senior project managers who each work directly with a state and system integrator counterpart.

Contract Required Qualifications For The Senior Project Manager Role

Requires a minimum of seven (7) years of broad, extensive and increasingly responsible experience applying PM principles, methods, techniques, and tools. At least four (4) years of that experience must have been as a senior PM of one or more large or complex IT projects.

Possession of (a) a bachelor’s degree, and (b) a valid Project Management Professional (PMP) certification from the Project Management Institute (PMI)

Additional qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis. The PMP certification is required and may not be substituted with additional experience.

Additional Qualifications

The Senior PM role requires proven project management skills in a highly complex and large-scale IT implementation. The successful candidate will need to work well in a dynamic environment, providing exceptional client service with outstanding professionalism. The role requires direct interaction with client and system integrator staff, as well as:

Strong analytical, organizational and core project management skills
Ability to help client personnel to leverage technology to solve business problems
Strong verbal and written communication skills with a commitment to client service and professionalism
Possess conceptual thinking skills, creativity and flexibility
Work well both independently and in a team
Must be self-sufficient and have the ability to self-manage
Experienced and comfortable in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio)
Ability to learn quickly and adapt with other technology applications in day-to-day work

Other

Candidates will need to complete and pass a background check conducted by SCO prior to beginning work
Remote work is allowed, but staff must be based in the continental United States. With advance notice, project staff will occasionally need to travel to Sacramento for project meetings.
Normal working hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific time. All staff, regardless of location, are required to perform duties within those hours.

We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Crowe, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,400.00 - $205,300.00 per year.

What does that mean for you? As Program Manager, you get the chance to:
Own end-to-end delivery of the Faridabad and Kurukshetra programs
: cohort planning, enrolment pipeline, batch scheduling, and the 800-learner target
Close and manage partnerships with colleges & NGOs whose female students/beneficiaries our program will upskill 

Lead and manage the on-ground field team
(including the Assistant Program Manager), setting weekly priorities and reviewing delivery quality
Coordinate with trainers, internal team, and on-ground stakeholders
to ensure smooth delivery.
Own program data and reporting
: operational trackers, impact dashboards, funder reports, and partnership reviews 

About Nimaya Foundation
Nimaya is a future-ready not-for-profit cofounded in 2021 by Navya Nanda and Samyak Chakrabarty, focused on preparing young women facing socio-economic barriers for a world of work being rapidly reshaped by AI and emerging technologies.

As GenAI transforms industries, workflows and hiring expectations, Nimaya works at the intersection of employability and AI readiness to ensure our Nimaya Naaris are not replaced by AI, but instead are equipped to participate and lead in this new economy
.
In partnership with institutions such as the Government of India's IndiaAI Mission
, we have enabled 10,000+ Nimaya Naaris across 6 states
to step into the new world of work with our flagship program - the GenAI Ready Naari.
Learn more about our mission and the impact we create!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D2q-qB-J1Dk
https://www.moneycontrol.com/entertainment/navya-naveli-nanda-launches-4th-edition-of-haryana-s-genai-ready-naari-programme-article-14011127.html
https://www.ptinews.com/story/entertainment/navya-nanda-and-samyak-chakrabarty-s-nimaya-partners-with-govt-s-ai-mission/3249973

Nimaya's GenAI Ready Naari Program

The GenAI Ready Naari Program equips young women with Generative AI skills and future-ready workplace competencies through 40 hours of immersive, hands-on learning
, out of which 32 hours are offline training and 8 hours are online. In these sessions, Naaris explore:
Building Chatbots & training Agentic AIs
AI-powered research & communication tactics
Creative problem-solving
Presentation & collaboration skills
Real-world projects & mentorship

The goal is not just to teach AI tools but to make learners truly future-ready for what the modern workplace demands: the ability to confidently work with AI instead of feeling threatened by it.

The Project you will join

If selected, you will step into the role of Program Manager of Haryana’s GenAI Ready Naari Program 

Over the next 2 years, this project aims to:
Upskill 800 young women across Faridabad and Kurukshetra

Expand GenAI learning to areas where access to AI exposure is still limited

Ensure meaningful learner outcomes beyond certification

What We're Looking For

Mindset

Sees CSR not as charity, but as a nation-building investment.
Obsessed with detail but driven by the big picture.
Proactive Attitude:
Willingness to take initiative and demonstrate adaptability.
Passion for Empowerment:
A strong desire to support and enable the success of young women from restrictive circumstances.

Background

4-5 years of experience
in program management, partnerships, or a related strategic role (development sector experience preferred)
Demonstrated experience managing or overseeing field/ops teams
, not just individual delivery
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
; strong stakeholder and partner management experience
Strong proficiency in Excel / Google Sheets
and comfort working with program data to build reports and presentations
Familiarity with compliance, documentation, and structured reporting systems
Strong communication skills in English and Hindi; 
Comfortable with travel
within Faridabad and Kurukshetra and occasional travel for partner/program engagements
Based in Faridabad/Kurukshetra (mandatory)

How to Apply

If you're a self-motivated individual eager to contribute to a meaningful cause, we encourage you to apply. Please send your CV to muskaan@nimaya.in. Use the subject line "Application: Program Manager, Haryana - [Your Name]" so we can track your application. Women candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

The opportunity

Your initial focus will be the transition of retained business capabilities into the client's technology environment as part of a business separation. You will lead delivery supporting infrastructure services and regulated metering, spanning lead management, customer enquiries, case management, help desk support and retailer enquiries.
Working across customer applications, contact centre solutions, digital platforms, integrations and vendor partners, you will oversee delivery from mobilisation through to operational transition. The role is expected to move into the Conversational AI project from around March 2027.

What you will lead

End-to-end delivery: mobilisation, design, implementation, testing, business readiness, cutover and closure.
Integrated delivery plans, budgets, resources, dependencies, risks and issues.
Collaboration across Customer, Technology, operations, business specialists and external vendors.
Customer service and retailer enquiry changes, including the applications and integrations that support them.
Vendor and commercial management, project governance and clear reporting to sponsors, steering committees and senior stakeholders.

What you will bring

Significant Senior Project Manager experience delivering complex technology-enabled business change.
A strong track record in customer-facing or customer-service technology initiatives.
Experience across several of these areas: CRM and customer service platforms, contact centre and telephony, digital/web applications, workflow and case management, enterprise integrations and APIs, or system migrations and technology transition.
Strong vendor and commercial management skills, with experience leading multidisciplinary business and technology teams.
Confidence engaging senior stakeholders, managing governance and steering committees, and resolving cross-functional delivery challenges.
Hands-on delivery experience across implementation, testing, cutover and operational readiness, with the ability to quickly understand new business domains and technologies.

Experience that will stand out

Conversational AI, chatbot or intelligent IVR delivery experience will be highly regarded, alongside contact centre, customer experience or customer operations expertise. Experience in workflow automation, process digitisation, CRM, SAP, contact centre or knowledge management platforms would also be valuable, as would an understanding of AI-enabled customer service and experience in utilities, energy or regulated industries.

Why consider this role?

Combine complex transition delivery with the opportunity to move into AI-enabled customer service. You will work across business and technology, lead multiple delivery partners, and bring your customer technology expertise to a Sydney-based hybrid contract role.
Interested?

new_jobs.title: CRM Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a CRM Project Manager based in the United States.

The CRM Project Manager will lead the successful delivery of CRM platform implementations and managed services for global clients. This role combines client relationship management, project planning, budget oversight, and cross-functional team coordination. You will manage projects of varying complexity, ensuring that deliverables, timelines, resources, and expectations remain aligned. Working closely with technical specialists and client stakeholders, you will guide projects through every stage of the delivery lifecycle, from onboarding and discovery to development and final delivery. You will also contribute to process improvements, project governance, and the continued development of CRM service offerings. This is an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful client engagements while supporting high-performing, internationally distributed teams.

Accountabilities

Responsibilities

You will oversee project execution from initial delivery handoff through completion, ensuring consistent communication, effective governance, and high-quality outcomes. Your responsibilities will include:

Serve as the primary client contact following the pre-sales handoff, leading engagements, facilitating meetings, and managing stakeholder expectations.
Lead multiple small- to medium-sized projects with low to moderate complexity, or manage a higher-complexity project on a fully allocated basis.
Develop and maintain project plans, track milestones and allocated hours, and oversee budgets and delivery progress.
Communicate project status, risks, issues, and dependencies clearly to clients and internal stakeholders.
Coordinate cross-functional teams, including architects, developers, consultants, data analysts, and lifecycle strategists, ensuring alignment with project objectives and delivery standards.
Identify discrepancies between discovery requirements and signed Statements of Work (SOWs), assess scope and assumption gaps, and propose structured resolutions, including Change Requests when needed.
Own execution across the five core delivery phases: Onboard, Discover, Design, Develop, and Deliver, ensuring that milestone exit criteria are met.
Manage client escalations effectively, involving senior internal stakeholders when additional support or decisions are required.
Provide actionable feedback to project team members and, where applicable, support their professional development through direct leadership.
Monitor team capacity, resource availability, and cross-functional dependencies to anticipate delivery challenges and mitigate risks.
Maintain standardized project documentation and governance tools, including RAID logs, Decision Trackers, JIRA boards, and shared repositories.
Follow established PMO processes, contribute feedback and recommendations for continuous improvement, and support consistent project management practices.
Communicate service capabilities and value propositions to clients while contributing to practice development, thought leadership, training, and industry events.
Stay informed about project management methodologies, professional development opportunities, and relevant market trends.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines strong project management expertise with experience delivering CRM and enterprise platform solutions. You should be comfortable managing client relationships, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, and taking ownership of complex delivery processes. Key qualifications include:

At least 5 years of relevant project management experience in CRM and enterprise platform implementations or CRM managed services.
Strong organizational, planning, and time-management skills, with excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously or coordinating projects involving several workstreams.
Proven ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and manage relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders.
Experience organizing and facilitating structured project kickoffs, discovery workshops, stakeholder meetings, and formal SOW gap reviews.
Ability to oversee small, cross-functional teams, monitor resource capacity, and proactively manage risks, issues, and dependencies.
Strong understanding of project lifecycle management, scope alignment, milestone tracking, and delivery governance.
Familiarity with JIRA or comparable project management platforms and the ability to maintain clear, consistent project documentation.
Ability to learn independently and pursue relevant professional certifications, accreditations, and platform credentials.
Flexibility to work hours aligned with the NAMER region, with priority given to Eastern Time (EST).

Additional Qualifications That Are Considered An Advantage

Certifications such as Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), or Salesforce Administrator.
Experience managing vendors and integrating third-party partners into project delivery.
Advanced proficiency in project management tools, including complex JIRA workflows and reporting.
Strong cross-cultural communication skills and experience working with geographically distributed client teams.

Benefits

Annual salary range of $70,000–$85,000 USD.
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance with full coverage.
Generous paid time off (PTO).
15 company-wide holidays.
401(k) retirement plan with company contributions.
Paid parental leave.
Work-life balance and a strong emphasis on employee well-being.
Career development opportunities in an innovative and evolving industry.
Opportunities to pursue entrepreneurial initiatives and grow professionally within a global network.
An internationally diverse and inclusive workplace, supported by employee resource groups and ongoing diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives.

We use an AI-powered matching process
to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. new_jobs.title: Public Sector Strategy Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:

At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.

In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence

About The Role

The California State Controller’s Office (SCO) is currently implementing a large and complex SaaS solution to support the California State Payroll System (CSPS) project. CSPS is a massive project, and the implementation includes both Personnel and Payroll functionality to support the needs of some 300,000 employees across 160 agencies and 21 bargaining units. With an estimated project budget exceeding $1 billion and staffing approaching 200 IT professionals, this highly complex effort is expected to continue for the next several years.

Description

The Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for execution, maintenance and enhancement of the CSPS Project Management Plans.

PMO responsibilities include:

ensuring that formal PM processes are in place and followed across all project workstreams (leadership, functional, technical, and organizational change management)
ensuring documentation is maintained in accordance with policy and procedure
regular periodic reporting on project risks, issues, and overall health, including stakeholder presentations as needed
assisting the CSPS Leadership Team in monitoring system integrator performance
providing analysis and recommendations for improvements to project management processes

The CSPS PMO is currently staffed by four senior project managers who each work directly with a state and system integrator counterpart.

Contract Required Qualifications For The Senior Project Manager Role

Requires a minimum of seven (7) years of broad, extensive and increasingly responsible experience applying PM principles, methods, techniques, and tools. At least four (4) years of that experience must have been as a senior PM of one or more large or complex IT projects.

Possession of (a) a bachelor’s degree, and (b) a valid Project Management Professional (PMP) certification from the Project Management Institute (PMI)

Additional qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis. The PMP certification is required and may not be substituted with additional experience.

Additional Qualifications

The Senior PM role requires proven project management skills in a highly complex and large-scale IT implementation. The successful candidate will need to work well in a dynamic environment, providing exceptional client service with outstanding professionalism. The role requires direct interaction with client and system integrator staff, as well as:

Strong analytical, organizational and core project management skills
Ability to help client personnel to leverage technology to solve business problems
Strong verbal and written communication skills with a commitment to client service and professionalism
Possess conceptual thinking skills, creativity and flexibility
Work well both independently and in a team
Must be self-sufficient and have the ability to self-manage
Experienced and comfortable in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio)
Ability to learn quickly and adapt with other technology applications in day-to-day work

Other

Candidates will need to complete and pass a background check conducted by SCO prior to beginning work
Remote work is allowed, but staff must be based in the continental United States. With advance notice, project staff will occasionally need to travel to Sacramento for project meetings.
Normal working hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific time. All staff, regardless of location, are required to perform duties within those hours.

We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Crowe, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,400.00 - $205,300.00 per year.

Our Benefits:

Your exceptional people experience starts here. At Crowe, we know that great people are what makes a great firm. We care about our people and offer employees a comprehensive total rewards package. Learn more about what working at Crowe can mean for you!

How You Can Grow:

We will nurture your talent in an inclusive culture that values diversity. You will have the chance to meet on a consistent basis with your Career Coach that will guide you in your career goals and aspirations. Learn more about where talent can prosper!

More about Crowe:

Crowe provides professional services through two separate entities: Crowe LLP delivers audit and attest services, and Crowe Advisory LLC provides tax, advisory, consulting, and other nonattest services.

The Crowe Global network consists of more than 300 independent accounting and advisory services firms in more than 150 countries around the globe, making it one of the largest accounting networks in the world*. As independent members of Crowe Global, Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC serve clients worldwide. (*As of July 2026)

Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC (and their respective subsidiary entities) provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetics, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Crowe LLP and Crowe Advisory LLC (and their respective subsidiary entities) does not accept unsolicited candidates, referrals or resumes from any staffing agency, recruiting service, sourcing entity or any other third-party paid service at any time. Any referrals, resumes or candidates submitted to Crowe, or any employee or owner of Crowe without a pre-existing agreement signed by both parties covering the submission will be considered the property of Crowe, and free of charge.

Crowe will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act.

Please visit our webpage to see notices of the various state and local Ban-the-Box laws and Fair Chance Ordinances, where applicable.

We are committed to a merit-based hiring process, evaluating all candidates consistently using objective, job-related criteria such as relevant experience, demonstrated skills, measurable impact, and alignment with the role’s responsibilities, and making employment decisions in a fair and inclusive manner free from discrimination.

If you are interested in applying for employment with Crowe and are in need of an accommodation or require special assistance to navigate our website or to complete your application, please visit our Applicant Assistance and Accommodations page for more information: https://careers.crowe.com/crowe-applicant-assistance-and-accommodation

About ELMO STUDIOS

ELMO STUDIOS is a boutique architecture and interior design practice based in New York City. The studio takes a fully integrated approach, treating architecture and interiors as inseparable parts of a single design vision. Rooted in a philosophy of refined minimalism, the work is defined by clarity, precision, and material integrity. At its core, the studio is driven by curiosity and a commitment to innovation — continually rethinking how space is inhabited and experienced. Projects are carried through all phases, from concept to construction, with a focus on thoughtful design and lasting impact.

The Role

The Project Manager will lead two to three projects concurrently, depending on scale and complexity, serving as the sole point of contact across all phases of each project. The role encompasses communication, timelines, deliverables, and coordination from early concept through construction administration.
While ELMO STUDIOS works across residential, retail, hospitality, and select office projects, this position requires substantial prior experience in high-end residential architecture in New York City. A strong design sensibility — across both architecture and interiors — is essential. The role calls for someone who balances leadership with hands-on engagement, contributing meaningfully to design development while managing complex workflows and external coordination.

Key Responsibilities

Manage two to three projects concurrently, depending on scale and complexity
Serve as the sole representative of ELMO STUDIOS across all phases of assigned projects
Direct internal team members and schedules to meet project milestones and deliverables
Lead the development, coordination, and issuance of high-quality construction drawing sets
Run meetings with clients, consultants, general contractors, and sub-consultants
Review and respond to RFIs, submittals, shop drawings, and related construction documentation
Conduct weekly site visits to monitor progress and ensure alignment with the design intent
Maintain project schedules, anticipating risks and coordinating across all parties involved

Qualifications

Minimum six years' experience in high-end residential architecture, including built work overseen in New York City
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Architecture or Interior Design from an accredited university (Master's preferred)
Strong design sensibility across both architecture and interiors, with a clear understanding of design history, precedent, and materials
Advanced technical knowledge of construction methods, MEP systems, and architectural detailing, particularly in residential and hospitality work
Proven ability to develop and manage complete construction drawing sets and documentation
Excellent organizational and project management skills, with the capacity to coordinate large teams and complex deliverables
Confidence representing the studio independently and leading collaboration with consultants and contractors
Proficiency in Rhino, Revit, Adobe Creative Suite, Office 365, and Google Workspace, including the ability to produce presentation-quality renderings in Rhino and Enscape
Self-directed curiosity and initiative, quick to adopt new tools, and inclined to improve the way the studio works day to day
Authorized to work in the U.S.

Site Presence & Mobility

The role requires regular site visits and active participation throughout construction. Candidates must be comfortable navigating active construction sites, including walk-throughs, contractor meetings, and field reviews. The ability to move efficiently across New York City — by subway, rideshare, or otherwise — is essential to supporting site coordination and client meetings in multiple boroughs.
This is a full-time, in-office position based in New York City, with attendance at the studio five days per week.

Please complete the application form via the following link
Elmo Studios: Job Application
and upload your résumé and portfolio.
As part of the form, you will be asked to share the names of three architects or designers you admire
, along with a brief note on why their work resonates with you.
Selected candidates may be invited to participate in a multi-stage interview process, including a practical design or visualization exercise.

new_jobs.title: Senior United States Operations Strategy Manager
new_jobs.description:
About The Department

The Strategy & Executive Office (SEO) organization is responsible for setting the short, mid, and long-term strategy for Novo Nordisk, Inc and ensures flawless execution of our key priorities. This encompasses long-term strategic planning, empowering and supporting leaders to successfully execute on strategic priorities, as well as driving and delivering high impact enterprise and business unit projects deemed critical to our future success. Furthermore, the Executive Office is responsible for supporting the President of NNI directly to ensure the pull through of priorities to set the direction for the entire organization.

The Position

Responsible for managing defined parts of strategy processes (both development, activation and implementation) of the overall company strategy for US Operations (USO) to drive sustainable growth. You will manage parts of the enterprise level strategy, ensuring together with your leaders that strategic ambition, priorities and enablers are connected and translated throughout the organization. In this role you will support defining USO's future direction, use scenario planning and stress testing to evaluate alternatives and surface trade-offs to help senior leaders make the hard choices that secure a sustainable, high impact future. You will convert strategic priorities into actionable initiatives with clear owners, timelines and success metrics, embed change management to drive adoption and partner with Finance to align investments and track benefits. Acting as the bridge across commercial, medical, access, supply and operations, you will ensure all parts of the value chain come together under one cohesive strategy, working closely with the Director, US Operations Strategy, to integrate strategic shifts into our strategy management processes.

Relationships

Reports to Director, US Operations Strategy. Internal interactions may include Executive Team, Executive Office, USO Lleadership, functional leads, Corporate Strategy and other HQ counterparts to ensure strategic coordination across Novo Nordisk. External relationships may include interactions with various subject matter experts and vendors based on the needs of special projects or implementation of new programs.

Essential Functions

Company level strategy ownership: manage selected parts of the US Operations (USO strategy, maintaining the central strategy repository, governance cadence and alignment between strategic ambition, priorities and organizational enablers

Project Managed workstreams under the strategic roadmap development: create and evolve parts of the 3–5 years strategic roadmap that defines USO’s future direction, identifies enterprise opportunities and aligns mid /long term ambitions with business priorities

Ecosystem insight and risk assessment: monitor the healthcare ecosystem (regulatory, technology, market, competitor) and translate external trends into strategic implications; identify and assess enterprise risks and recommend mitigations

Scenario planning and decision support: build the assumptions supporting scenario modeling, sensitivity analysis and stress testing to evaluate alternatives, surface trade-offs and provide clear recommendations to enable senior leaders to make high impact choices for benefits of our patients

Strategy activation and initiative delivery: support convert strategic priorities into actionable initiatives and operating plans with clear owners, timelines, success metrics and delivery governance; lead cross functional workstreams to achieve results

Change management and adoption: design and embed change management approaches (communications, training, stakeholder engagement) to ensure organizational readiness and sustained adoption of strategic shifts

Financial alignment: partner with Finance to ensure alignment between strategy and financial milestones, to accurately translate strategy into investment guidance for the company

Performance measurement and continuous improvement: support line of business in defining KPIs and dashboards, monitor execution performance, recommend course corrections and drive continuous improvement of strategy processes and tools

Stakeholder influence: build alignment across commercial, medical, access, supply, operations, represent USO strategy in senior leadership forums and convene the US Operations Strategy Board for cross value chain decisions

Communication and strategic reporting: develop audience appropriate strategy communications and presentation materials for executive and management audiences; partner with Executive Communications as needed

Team dynamics: foster a collaborative, accountable culture; coach and mentor colleagues; ensure close partnership with the Director, US Operations Strategy to integrate strategic shifts into the broader strategy management process

Physical Requirements

10-20% overnight travel required.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree from an accredited university or equivalent education with 7+ years of experience in progressively relevant corporate business strategy development and planning, marketing and brand management, consulting, commercial operations experience required; pharmaceutical or CPG industries strongly preferred

Master's Degree/MBA from an accredited university or equivalent education with 5+ years of experience and/or Doctorate degree from an accredited university or equivalent education with 3+ years of experience

Business case development, management consulting, strategy, or finance experience preferred

Understanding of the external marketplace and familiarity in metabolic disease areas preferred

Strategic thinker with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work with senior management and communicate effectively to the highest level of executives

Strong decision-making skills through demonstrated ability to leverage evidenced-based insights and sound judgement into strategy development, deployment and optimization

Project Management, Process Development And Change Management Experience Required

Ability to manage competing priorities; strong organizational skills; demonstrated ability to streamline and simplify complex concepts for broader audience

Proven cross-functional organizational behaviour and collaboration skills with ability to influence and inspire multiple levels of leadership

People Management/team Development Experience Preferred

The base compensation range for this position is $120,000 to $220,000. Base compensation is determined based on a number of factors. This position is also eligible for a company bonus based on individual and company performance. Novo Nordisk offers long-term incentive compensation and or company vehicles depending on the position's level or other company factors.

Employees are also eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs including medical, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; disability insurance; 401(k) savings plan; flexible spending accounts; employee assistance program; tuition reimbursement program; and voluntary benefits such as group legal, critical illness, identity theft protection, pet insurance and auto/home insurance. The Company also offers time off pursuant to its sick time policy, flex-able vacation policy and parental leave policy.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

At Novo Nordisk, we're not chasing quick fixes – we're creating lasting change for long-term health. For over 100 years, we've been driven by a single purpose: to defeat serious chronic diseases and help millions of people live healthier lives. This dedication fuels our constant curiosity and inspires us to push the boundaries of what's possible in healthcare. We embrace diverse perspectives, seek out bold ideas, and build partnerships rooted in shared purpose. Together, we're making healthcare more accessible, treating and defeating diseases, and pioneering solutions that create change spanning generations. When you join us, you become part of something bigger – a legacy of impact that reaches far beyond today.

Novo Nordisk is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by local, state or federal laws, rules or regulations.

Job Description:

What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence

About The Role

The California State Controller’s Office (SCO) is currently implementing a large and complex SaaS solution to support the California State Payroll System (CSPS) project. CSPS is a massive project, and the implementation includes both Personnel and Payroll functionality to support the needs of some 300,000 employees across 160 agencies and 21 bargaining units. With an estimated project budget exceeding $1 billion and staffing approaching 200 IT professionals, this highly complex effort is expected to continue for the next several years.

Description

The Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for execution, maintenance and enhancement of the CSPS Project Management Plans.

PMO responsibilities include:

ensuring that formal PM processes are in place and followed across all project workstreams (leadership, functional, technical, and organizational change management)
ensuring documentation is maintained in accordance with policy and procedure
regular periodic reporting on project risks, issues, and overall health, including stakeholder presentations as needed
assisting the CSPS Leadership Team in monitoring system integrator performance
providing analysis and recommendations for improvements to project management processes

The CSPS PMO is currently staffed by four senior project managers who each work directly with a state and system integrator counterpart.

Contract Required Qualifications For The Senior Project Manager Role

Requires a minimum of seven (7) years of broad, extensive and increasingly responsible experience applying PM principles, methods, techniques, and tools. At least four (4) years of that experience must have been as a senior PM of one or more large or complex IT projects.

Possession of (a) a bachelor’s degree, and (b) a valid Project Management Professional (PMP) certification from the Project Management Institute (PMI)

Additional qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis. The PMP certification is required and may not be substituted with additional experience.

The Senior PM role requires proven project management skills in a highly complex and large-scale IT implementation. Strong analytical, organizational and core project management skills
Ability to help client personnel to leverage technology to solve business problems
Strong verbal and written communication skills with a commitment to client service and professionalism
Possess conceptual thinking skills, creativity and flexibility
Work well both independently and in a team
Must be self-sufficient and have the ability to self-manage
Experienced and comfortable in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio)
Ability to learn quickly and adapt with other technology applications in day-to-day work

Position Title

Senior Business Analyst

Location:

Washington, DC (Hybrid)

Clearance Requirements

Public Trust

Pay Rate

$55.00 - $65 per hour on W2, depending on qualifications and experience

Position Description

We are seeking a Senior Business Analyst to help Government customers understand operational challenges and turn complex or loosely defined problems into clear requirements. You will lead discovery, investigate how work happens in practice, and develop findings that help customers make informed decisions about process and system improvements.

The Senior Business Analyst independently translates the scope, objectives, and constraints in a statement of work into a practical discovery and requirements-gathering plan. Working with the Project Manager and project team, this role designs and leads interviews and workshops, maps business processes, analyzes findings, and develops validated requirements. The analyst also provides direction and feedback to junior analysts.

Responsibilities

Interpret the statement of work and available background information to define discovery objectives, identify information gaps, and develop a sequenced plan aligned with the engagement scope and deliverables.
Independently select and design the requirements-gathering approach based on the problem, stakeholder groups, and operational context, identifying assumptions or scope questions that require customer clarification.
Design workshop structures, including objectives, participants, agendas, facilitation activities, and expected outputs, to investigate processes and reconcile differing perspectives. Develop tailored interview guides and reusable discovery templates.
Lead interviews and facilitate workshops, asking focused questions to uncover unstated needs, exceptions, workarounds, and differences between documented procedures and actual practice. Adapt the approach as findings emerge.
Map and analyze business processes across teams, documenting decision points, handoffs, responsibilities, dependencies, and bottlenecks.
Research relevant policies, procedures, existing documentation, and available operational evidence. Analyze findings across sources to identify themes, conflicting accounts, underlying causes, and improvement opportunities.
Translate validated findings into clear, specific, and verifiable business and system requirements, distinguishing underlying needs from proposed solutions and maintaining the connection to supporting evidence.
Verify requirements for clarity, consistency, completeness, and evidentiary support. Validate process documentation and requirements with stakeholders to confirm they reflect actual operations, business needs, and intended outcomes.
Present evidence-based findings and recommendations, identifying assumptions and unresolved questions. Review and guide junior analysts' work.
Use approved AI tools to improve the efficiency of research, analysis, and documentation. Independently verify AI-assisted outputs against source evidence, correct errors and unsupported conclusions, and follow applicable customer and company data-handling requirements.
Additional responsibilities include supporting growth and proposal efforts, as well as expanding business within your assigned portfolio.

Required Skills/Education

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Experience supporting Government customers or working in environments where policies and organizational responsibilities shape operations. Experience analyzing processes that involve multiple teams or organizations, and familiarity with process-mapping and requirements-management tools.

Work Experience Requirements

Five or more years of relevant experience in business analysis, requirements development, or business process improvement.
Demonstrated experience independently planning and leading discovery from a statement of work or similarly defined engagement scope, including designing workshops and selecting requirements-gathering methods without step-by-step direction.
Proven ability to analyze ambiguous or conflicting information, develop process maps, and translate operational findings into actionable requirements.
Strong research and analytical skills, including evaluating sources, testing assumptions, and identifying missing evidence.
Clear written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain findings to business and technical audiences.
Sound judgment in working with customers, completing assigned analysis activities, and raising issues that require a decision.
Practical experience using AI tools in analysis and documentation, with the ability to evaluate outputs, verify supporting evidence, and perform the underlying business analysis independently of AI.

Education Requirements

A bachelor's degree in business, information systems, public administration, or a related field is preferred, not required. Candidates without a degree are encouraged to apply if their professional experience demonstrates the required analytical, research, and communication skills and they meet the work experience requirements.
